tasks.short: Inform citizens of community services and recommend options

steps.what: Discuss the citizen's needs and immediate safety concerns
Look up current community services and check practical referral requirements
Recommend appropriate options and explain access and next steps to citizens

tasks.design: Configure searchable service cards in {DOCS} using service area and topic filters. The officer checks currency and fit before recommending options; the tool makes no eligibility or safety decision.
tasks.previous_blocker: Service details are distributed across documents and become stale.
tasks.enabler_now: Native document metadata and search can narrow the reference material.
tasks.still_hard: A nominally available service may not fit the person's needs or current capacity.
tasks.human_edge: Listen, recognise urgency and explain realistic choices without promising access.
tasks.altitude: Less directory hunting, with unchanged recommendation authority.

evidence.claim: A deterministic service-directory search and its savings are an E1 scenario; no matching measured case is supplied.

assumptions: Boundary is officer discussion, service lookup and advice; provider intake is outside it.

Officer produces topic and area filters during retained s2 time from needs understood in s1. Service liaison produces service name, coverage, contact, opening hours, referral requirements, source and checked date; four incremental other-role hours fund verification and metadata capture.
Missing or stale information requires officer manual lookup or a call within retained s2 time, with no inferred eligibility.
Use native search before code; personal case details need not enter directory search.
unknowns: Lawful access and local referral arrangements
research_questions: Does filtered search halve lookup time after failed searches and freshness checks?

already_counted.description: Query capture, freshness checks and manual fallback

incremental.description: Maintain officer-facing filters and report stale cards
Service liaison captures and verifies directory metadata

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=87.5, gross=12.5 minus 3 focal upkeep gives net=9.5. High assumes reusable service cards; low assumes only 3 lookup hours saved. All 75 discussion and advice hours remain; other-role upkeep is reported separately.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Gather current assignments, incidents and staffing information for supervision
Supervise law enforcement staff, resolve operational issues and direct safe work

tasks.design: Configure a current assignment view in {OPS_SYSTEM}, with links to source records in {DOCS}. Use it for preparation while keeping direction, welfare checks and intervention with the supervising officer.
tasks.previous_blocker: Current assignments and incidents must be collected across existing screens.
tasks.enabler_now: Native views can group existing records by shift and assignment.
tasks.still_hard: The view cannot establish whether a direction is safe or lawful in current conditions.
tasks.human_edge: Notice fatigue, uncertainty and conflict that status fields do not capture.
tasks.altitude: The officer spends less time gathering records and retains all supervisory decisions.

reach.learn: How to combine records with direct welfare observations

evidence.claim: A native assignment view is an E1 design and does not establish automated supervisory judgement or measured savings.
The digest identifies Dutch works-council consent concerns when systems monitor staff; applicability needs local assessment.

assumptions: Boundary is patrol-officer supervisory work, excluding a separate supervisor's labour and staff execution time.

Existing dispatchers produce assignment identifier, shift, assigned officer, status and update time in operational records. Incident authors maintain incident identifier and source link. Existing capture remains unchanged; no new reporting or staff scoring is requested.
Supervising officer selects shift and verifies sources in retained s1 time. Missing or stale status requires direct enquiry in that time.
Test native views first. Two focal hours fund view and access upkeep; no model processes police records.
unknowns: Whether the officer has supervisory duties
Record access, staff consultation and source freshness
research_questions: Can one view reduce gathering by 40% without creating new status-reporting work?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=92, gross=8 minus 2 upkeep gives net=6. High assumes reliable native views; low assumes only 2 gathering hours saved. All 80 supervision hours remain.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Process prisoners and maintain booking and status records

steps.what: Process prisoner intake and capture verified identity, booking facts and authorised status
Copy verified booking facts into related booking and status records
Verify populated records, correct mismatches and maintain authorised prisoner status changes

tasks.design: Use native booking-record reuse in {OPS_SYSTEM} to populate related internal records from one verified capture. The officer retains physical processing, identity checks, record reconciliation and every authorised custody-status change; copied fields cannot order detention or release.
tasks.previous_blocker: The same verified facts may be keyed into several internal records.
tasks.enabler_now: Native field reuse can remove duplicate entry when the booking system supports it.
tasks.still_hard: Identity conflicts, legal authority and changing prisoner needs require human resolution.
tasks.human_edge: Treat prisoners safely and respectfully while checking facts against authority.
tasks.altitude: Less duplicate entry, with unchanged custody authority and verification duties.

reach.learn: Record linkage and auditable correction procedures

evidence.claim: Single capture and native field reuse are an E1 booking design; the digest does not establish a measured booking case.
The digest identifies Dutch police-data constraints on solely automated adverse decisions and high-risk processing; local legal review is needed.

assumptions: Boundary covers officer intake, duplicate record entry and status maintenance; other custody staff work is excluded.

Officer in s1 produces prisoner reference, verified name and identity source, booking reference, intake time and authorised initial status with authority reference. All initial capture remains in 40 full hours; s3 captures and verifies every later status event with time and authority reference in 35 full hours.

Native reuse copies exact fields only into internal provisional records; s3 checks them before use. Missing identifiers or failed mapping route to manual entry in retained s3 time. No identity matching guess, release action or detention decision is automated.
Only documented duplicate entry earns savings; existing automatic population earns none. Test native configuration before integration code.
unknowns: Actual duplicate-entry share and native field-reuse support
Permitted record destinations, audit rules and access
research_questions: Can the system remove duplicate entry without reducing intake, status verification or correction time?

already_counted.description: Initial processing and structured fact capture
Reconciliation, fallback entry and authorised status capture

incremental.description: Check field mappings, access and failed transfers

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=75, gross=25 minus 4 focal upkeep gives net=21. High requires 25 hours of real duplicate entry; low assumes only 4 hours removable. Intake and status work retain 75 hours; technical upkeep is separate.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Locate and confiscate property as directed by court order

steps.what: Read court order and verify authority, property description and execution limits
Locate property and confirm it matches the court order
Confiscate confirmed property within court authority and safeguard it

tasks.design: Keep court-order interpretation, identification and confiscation with the authorised officer. {DOCS} remains the source of the order; no machine extraction is allowed to expand its scope.
tasks.previous_blocker: Execution requires legal judgement and physical identification and control.
tasks.enabler_now: No demonstrated reduction in this task is proposed.
tasks.still_hard: Disputed ownership and ambiguous property descriptions require escalation.
tasks.human_edge: Exercise lawful discretion and de-escalate contested encounters.
tasks.altitude: Decision rights and field duties remain unchanged.

reach.learn: How to resolve unclear descriptions before action

evidence.claim: Retaining interpretation and physical confiscation is an E1 task-design judgement, without a saving claim.

assumptions: Boundary is officer review, location and confiscation; court issuance and later disposal are outside it.
The court supplies the authoritative order. No structured input or automatic decision is introduced; the officer reads the source in s1.
No implementation is proposed, so native configuration and incremental upkeep are unnecessary.
unknowns: Jurisdiction and officer authority to execute the order
research_questions: What is the required escalation route when the order does not uniquely identify property?

already_counted.description: Authority verification, location and confiscation retained

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100, upkeep=0 and net=0. No separate paperwork baseline is invented.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Service lookup, supervisory preparation and duplicate booking entry may shrink; all legal and interpersonal decisions remain with officers.
reach: Police records officer: auditable booking corrections
role.ambitious_version: Provide reliable community guidance and accurate custody records while preserving direct responsibility for coercive actions.
